4 Bounds in terms of other well-known graph parameters




In this section, we consider bounds, some verified and some suspected, on the graph parameter ν⁡(G)\nu(G). We denote the chromatic number of a graph GG by χ⁡(G)\chi(G). It is well known that every graph GG contains a subgraph whose minimum degree is at least χ⁡(G)−1\chi(G)-1, that is, l⁡(G)≥χ⁡(G)−1l(G)\geq\chi(G)-1. The Hadwiger number, η⁡(G)\eta(G), of a graph GG is the largest integer tt such that the complete graph KtK_{t} is a minor of GG. Consequently, it is clear that ⌈κ⌉​(G)≥η⁡(G)−1\lceil\kappa\rceil(G)\geq\eta(G)-1, and hence by Theorem 1.6 ν⁡(G)≥η⁡(G)−1\nu(G)\geq\eta(G)-1. One of the most famous conjectures in graph theory is ‘Hadwiger’s conjecture’ which asserts that η⁡(G)≥χ⁡(G)\eta(G)\geq\chi(G). Therefore, if either δ\delta-Conjecture 1.5 or Hadwiger’s Conjecture is true, then ν⁡(G)≥χ⁡(G)−1\nu(G)\geq\chi(G)-1. However, to the best of these authors’ knowledge, the validity of this inequality in general remains an open problem. We thus state it here as a conjecture:



Conjecture 4.1.



For any graph GG, we have ν⁡(G)≥χ⁡(G)−1\nu(G)\geq\chi(G)-1.





Using the following recent result by Nguyen [30] and Theorem 1.6, one can observe that, ν⁡(G)\nu(G) is near to one-third of the value predicted by Conjecture 4.1.



Theorem 4.2 (Nguyen [30]).



For every integer k≥1k\geq 1, every graph GG with χ⁡(G)≥4916⋅k\chi(G)\geq\frac{49}{16}\cdot k contains a (k+1)(k+1)-connected subgraph with more than χ⁡(G)−k\chi(G)-k vertices and chromatic number at least χ⁡(G)−2​k+2\chi(G)-2k+2.




Corollary 4.3.
